newsitem.title: INDIA: India's PM says no regret leaving office.
newsitem.headline: India's PM says no regret leaving office.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said on Friday that he would have no regret leaving office and that he was prepared to face the electorate in snap polls.
"There is no regret to vacate this office, to lay down this office," Deve Gowda told the lower house of parliament at the conclusion of debate on a vote of confidence in his government.

Deve Gowda referred frequently to Congress party president Sitaram Kesri, who announced he was withdrawing his party's make-or-break support for the prime minister's United Front coalition on March 30, triggering the confidence vote.

"I have been branded as inefficient by the Congress president," Deve Gowda said. "The final judgement...is before the nation of 950 million people. The inefficient prime minister will go before the nation."
The prime minister said it was no use trying to "patch up" with the Congress as it would serve no purpose.
"We don't want elections but we see no alternative road," Deve Gowda said.
